skill.name: executor-critique
skill.description: Audit initiative artifacts against upstream documents, route scoped repairs, and require independent re-audits before clearing a phase.
skill.summary: Coordinate independent artifact reviews, scoped repairs, and evidence-based phase clearance.
skill.author: atri10

security_audit.summary: All 162 static alerts are false positives: Markdown formatting, ordinary review questions, and fixed helper references. One semantic finding identifies conflicting repair-log ownership that can lose audit evidence when multiple artifact repairers are dispatched. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or exfiltration; helper implementations are outside this package and remain unverified.

remediation.issue: Multiple artifact repairers receive conflicting exclusive ownership of the same component-round repair log.
remediation.suggestion: Assign each artifact a unique repair log and aggregate those logs in the controller. Alternatively, use one designated log writer with serialized updates.

content.value_statement: Conflicting documents can carry incorrect decisions into later development phases. This skill coordinates independent audits, scoped repairs, and fresh re-audits before phase clearance.
actual_capabilities: Provides component check catalogs for charter, discovery, architecture, design, specification, plans, code, verification, and handoff.
Defines independent auditor, artifact repairer, and fresh re-auditor prompt templates.
Requires quoted evidence and file locations for component, cross-artifact, and upstream contract findings.
Directs repairers to edit only their assigned artifact and repair log, without committing changes.
Requires re-auditors to inspect repair diffs, verify closure, and flag weakened requirements.
Documents helper-based phase checks, three-round escalation, and human-only waivers.
limitations: Required Executor helper scripts and related skills are not included in this four-file package.
Audits depend on complete component sets, upstream documents, and correctly filled dispatch placeholders.
Independent reviews require agent dispatch support; the prompts alone do not provide an execution engine.
Multiple artifact repairers need explicit repair-log ownership to avoid conflicting writes to the component-round log.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Charter
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the charter for [INITIATIVE_ID] using the charter catalog. Dispatch an independent auditor and require evidence for every finding.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review goals, non-goals, scope, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Specifications with Upstream Decisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the specification component for [INITIATIVE_ID]. Supply its complete artifact set, charter, active architecture decisions, and verification criteria.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: check traceability and contradictions across documents.

prompt_templates.title: Repair Assigned Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Repair [FINDING_IDS] in [ARTIFACT_FILE] from [AUDIT_FILE]. Preserve requirements, log evidence, and do not commit. Give each repairer a unique log.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: perform scoped fixes without weakening contracts or colliding with other repairers.

prompt_templates.title: Re-Audit the Final Round
prompt_templates.prompt: Dispatch a fresh R03 re-auditor for [INITIATIVE_ID] and [COMPONENT]. Supply prior findings, repair logs, and the repair diff. Escalate unresolved findings to a human.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: verify closure and enforce the three-audit limit.

output_examples.input: Audit a specification whose interface name differs from the architecture contract.
output: High finding H1: The specification and architecture use different names for the same interface.
Evidence: The audit quotes both conflicting passages and records their actual file locations.
Proposed repair: The controller identifies the authoritative contract and routes a fix to the incorrect document.

output_examples.input: Re-audit a repair that removed a requirement instead of satisfying it.
output: New high finding: The repair deleted the requirement and weakened the artifact.
Next step: Restore the requirement and repair its cause, or escalate for an explicit human decision.

output_examples.input: Start an audit when a required upstream document cannot be opened.
output: Reason: A required upstream document is missing or unreadable.
Next step: Supply the exact required document before dispatching the auditor again.

best_practices: Supply the complete artifact set and required upstream evidence before dispatching an auditor.
Use separate audit, repair, and re-audit agents, with explicit ownership for every artifact and repair log.
Verify quoted evidence, preserve unresolved findings, and run the documented helper check before reporting phase clearance.
anti_patterns: Letting the controller approve its own work or accepting a repair log as proof of closure.
Deleting requirements, weakening exact values, or granting an agent-created waiver to obtain a passing verdict.
Dispatching several artifact repairers with exclusive ownership of the same repair log.

faq.question: Which AI tools does this skill target?
faq.answer: The package targets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Execution requires an environment with agent dispatch support and the related Executor helpers.

faq.question: Does the package include its helper scripts?
faq.answer: No. It contains the skill document and three prompt templates. Helper implementations are referenced but are not included here.

faq.question: What makes an audit pass?
faq.answer: The documented contract requires zero HIGH and zero MEDIUM findings. The referenced helper checks reported verdicts against counts and supporting records.

faq.question: Can a repairer change upstream contracts?
faq.answer: No. Upstream contract findings belong to the controller, which must amend the source through an initiative ruling.

faq.question: How many audit rounds are allowed?
faq.answer: The workflow allows R01 through R03. Unresolved findings after R03 go to a human rather than another repair round.

faq.question: Can multiple artifacts be repaired independently?
faq.answer: The template assigns one repairer per artifact. Define separate repair logs or a designated log writer to prevent conflicting ownership.
